extraFacts.source: Parker Hannifin product page "Pneumatic NFPA Cylinder - 4MA Series" (ph.parker.com) and Parker tie-rod pneumatic cylinder catalogue 0900P-7 / 0900P Engineering Data (parker.com)

extraFacts.source: Parker Hannifin Pneumatic Cylinders series page (phdev.parker.com/us/en/pneumatic-cylinders) and tie-rod catalogue 0900P-7

extraFacts.fact: Pressure conversion: 1 bar = 14.5038 psi, so 250 psi is about 17 bar (17.2 bar).

Theoretical cylinder force = air pressure x effective piston area (area = pi/4 x bore squared; on the return stroke subtract the rod area). Piston areas: 1-1/2 in bore 1.77 sq in, 2 in 3.14, 2-1/2 in 4.91, 3-1/4 in 8.30, 4 in 12.57, 5 in 19.63, 6 in 28.27, 8 in 50.27. Extend force at 80 psi: 141, 251, 393, 664, 1,005, 1,571, 2,262 and 4,021 lbf. Retract force at 80 psi: 1-1/2 in bore with 5/8 in rod 117 lbf, with 1 in rod 79 lbf; 2 in bore 227 / 188 lbf; 2-1/2 in bore 368 / 330 lbf; 3-1/4 in bore with 1 in rod 601, with 1-3/8 in rod 545 lbf; 4 in bore 942 / 887 lbf; 5 in bore 1,508 / 1,452 lbf; 6 in bore with 1-3/8 in rod 2,143, with 1-3/4 in rod 2,070 lbf; 8 in bore 3,902 / 3,829 lbf. Real output is lower by seal friction; size with a load ratio margin.
extraFacts.source: F = P x A (basic fluid power); Parker 0900P Engineering Data cylinder force tables

extraFacts.fact: In Parker 4MA and 2MNR model numbers the code reads bore (1.50 = 1-1/2 in), optional C for a head-end cushion, the mounting letters, the series (4MA or 2MNR), piston/seal and port options, rod code, then the stroke in inches (02.00 = 2 in); a C at the end after A marks a cap-end cushion. faqs.q: What is a Parker 2MNR series 1-1/2 inch bore tie-rod air cylinder used for?
faqs.a: The Parker 2MNR 1-1/2" bore is an NFPA tie-rod air cylinder with a non-rotating piston design, so the rod does not turn as it strokes. It suits tooling, pushers and clamps where the rod end must keep its orientation; this listing carries 84 Parker part numbers with strokes from 0.25 to 20 in.

faqs.q: How do you read a Parker 2MNR part number such as 1.50CNB2MNRUT9AC01.00?
faqs.a: 1.50CNB2MNRUT9AC01.00 reads as bore 1.50 (1-1/2"), then the mounting letters, the series 2MNR, the piston and port options, and the stroke in inches at the end. A C straight after the bore adds a head-end cushion and a C after the final A a cap-end cushion. Mounting letters include J (MF1 head flange), H (MF2 cap flange), F (MS4 side tap) and NB (base bar).

faqs.q: What stroke lengths and mountings does the Parker 2MNR 1-1/2" bore cylinder come in?
faqs.a: Our Parker 2MNR 1-1/2" bore table runs from 0.25 in to 20 in stroke across 8 mounting styles, mainly side tap (MS4), head rectangular flange (MF1), cap rectangular flange (MF2) and no mount (MX0). Pick the stroke for the travel you need plus any over-travel, and the mounting that takes the load in line with the rod. Mounting choice is covered in our [cushioning and mounting guide](/blog/pneumatic-cylinder-cushioning-and-mounting).

faqs.q: How much force does a Parker 2MNR 1-1/2 inch bore cylinder give at 80 psi?
faqs.a: A 1-1/2" bore has a piston area of 1.77 sq in, so the 2MNR gives about 141 lbf theoretical extend force at 80 psi. Retract force is lower because the rod takes up part of the area, and friction takes a little more. Work through load ratio and air consumption with our [cylinder sizing guide](/blog/how-to-size-a-pneumatic-cylinder).

faqs.q: What is the maximum operating pressure of the Parker 2MNR 1-1/2" bore cylinder?
faqs.a: Parker rates the 2MNR series at 250 psi maximum on air, about 17 bar, and every rated row in this 1-1/2" bore table shows 250 psi. Most plant air runs well below that, so in practice the valve, tubing or regulator rating is usually the lower limit to check.

faqs.q: Can the Parker 2MNR 1-1/2 inch cylinder run on non-lubricated compressed air?

For any other medium, confirm with the maker before ordering.

faqs.q: Which standard does the Parker 2MNR 1-1/2" bore tie-rod cylinder follow?

NFPA fixes mounting interfaces, not a test standard, so ask for a certificate of conformity with the order if your project needs one.

faqs.q: What valves and fittings connect to a Parker 2MNR 1-1/2 inch air cylinder?
faqs.a: A double-acting 2MNR 1-1/2" bore needs a 5/2 or 5/3 directional valve, flow controls to set speed, and push-in or threaded fittings sized to its ports. Valves are on our [solenoid valves shelf](/c/pneumatic-solenoid-valves), and meter-out speed controls on the [flow controls shelf](/c/pneumatic-flow-check-valves).

faqs.q: How should a Parker 2MNR 1-1/2" bore cylinder be installed for long seal life?

Use an alignment coupler or pivot mount where the load moves off-line, keep the air clean and dry, and set any cushions so the piston does not hit the end caps at full speed.
